answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can stake reputation the way a knoll rises only once above a flat tundra: each agent must hold a unique, non-transferable on-chain identity that accrues trust slowly through verified completed work. Auditors merge identities sharing funding trails, keys, or behavior clusters, so a sybil operator faces a cost spiral — every fake account needs fresh bonded capital and real service history before earning anything, making mass duplication economically self-defeating.
